text:
Jordan Lee: heads up — multiple support escalations about p99 latency spikes starting ~03:00 UTC. Customers calling out slow API responses (time-to-first-byte >> usual). Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/latency/p99-overview (shared in thread). Acme and BrightApp reported timeouts/UX freezes. :rotating_light:

Priya Patel: I'm on it. observed p95 jumped from ~180ms -> ~700ms and p99 to ~2s on rwd-8b in us-west-2. Errors aren't HTTP 5xx, mostly slow responses (200s).

Sam Nguyen: grabbing traces. early signal looks like long wait in batching queue + grow in kv-cache miss rate. sending link to trace: https://traces.redwood/trace/abc123

Marta Rossi: can someone paste a repro curl? need to reproduce locally with emulated load.

Jordan Lee: quick repro we used from support:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-8b","input":""$(python -c 'print(\"x\"*3200)')"","max_tokens":1024,"stream":false}'
```
This hits large prompts + high concurrency from their integration. They said they ramp to ~200 concurrent requests.

Sam Nguyen: reproduced a small load test (50 concurrent) — median ok, but we see a fat tail when batch window grows. suspect batching heuristics cause head-of-line blocking for long prompts. logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T03:12:05Z] batch_enter queue_size=87 wait_ms=412 batch_window_ms=75
[2026-03-15T03:12:05Z] exec start kv_cache_miss=true kv_lookup_ms=1120 model_exec_ms=320
[2026-03-15T03:12:08Z] response send total_ms=3012
```

Marta Rossi: that kv_lookup_ms=1120 is surprising — are we hitting remote KVS (redis cluster) or slow HSM?

Priya Patel: preliminary: a shard of redis in us-west-2 had increased latency after config push at 02:50 (changed eviction policy). Could be contributing. Also batch_window_ms had been bumped to 75ms in a prior optimization. Combined effects amplify p99.

Luis Gomez: product impact: UX timeouts for webhooks and streaming clients. We need an immediate mitigation playbook (short term) + SLO guardrails (mid-term).

Priya Patel: immediate mitigations (doing now):
- reduce batch window: set batch_window_ms -> 10 for routes serving interactive customers
- enable per-route circuit breaker for rwd-8b to reject after 15% queue saturation
- add fallback routing: route traffic from us-west-2 -> us-east-1 for model rwd-8b for key customers (Acme, BrightApp)
- temporary per-api-key concurrency cap: max_concurrent_requests=12 for top noisy keys
- lower default max_tokens to 256 for host-level until stabilized

Applying routing change with admin API now:
```bash
# emergency route override to fallback region
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/route_override 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" 
 -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"rwd-8b","from_region":"us-west-2","to_region":"us-east-1","reason":"p99 spike 2026-03-15"}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy started for route override (job id: deploy-8743). Estimated 45s to roll.

Sam Nguyen: also flipping batch window via runtime API:
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://runtime.redwood.internal/v1/config/batching 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" 
 -d '{"batch_window_ms":10,"max_batch_size":64}'
```
Applied to pool: inference-pool-14.

Jordan Lee: Priya — can we add a short-term circuit breaker config sample? want to push to canary.

Marta Rossi: sample circuit breaker payload we use in playbooks: 
```json
{"circuit_breaker":{ "enabled":true, "failure_threshold":0.05, "consecutive_failures":10, "track_p99_ms":true, "p99_threshold_ms":1500, "action":"reject or fallback" }}
```
We can set action to "fallback" which will route to rwd-3b-quant if threshold exceeded.

Priya Patel: pushing CB to canary now (route id: r-2091) -> action=fallback,to_model=rwd-3b-quant.

Sam Nguyen: monitoring shows immediate drop in batch wait and p99 coming down to ~900ms after batch window change + fallback started. us-west-2 -> us-east-1 routing also shows fewer pending requests in us-west-2.

Jordan Lee: what about rate limits/guardrails to prevent noisy customers from causing cluster-wide p99 regressions?

Luis Gomez: propose SLO guardrails (mid-term):
- per-api-key concurrency cap default 20, adjustable per-customer with soft/strict modes
- token-budget enforcement: reject requests that would exceed token limit per minute with 429 and a clear retry-after
- automatic model-fallback policy when p95>350ms for 3m window
- strict circuit breakers that trigger fallback (rwd-3b-quant) or region failover
- alerting rule: fire pager when p99 > 2s for 5m across >30% of routes

Marta Rossi: technically implement with three components: control plane overrides, runtime circuit-breaker library, and routing policy agent. Need infra work but doable in a week for MVP.

Sam Nguyen: also recommend a short-term protective throttle: for requests with prompt_length > 2000 chars, return quick 429 with message recommending streaming or smaller prompts. Helps head-of-line blocking.

Jordan Lee: support repro step for engineers:
1) use the curl above with a 3k char prompt
2) run 100 concurrent sessions (wrk, vegeta or k6)
3) inspect /metrics and traces for batch_window_ms, queue_size, kv_lookup_latencies

Priya Patel: follow-ups assigned: 
- Priya: routing + batch config (in progress)
- Sam: tracing + postmortem notes (I'll collect traces + attach)
- Marta: implement emergency circuit-breaker template in runtime (ETA 48h)
- Luis: write SLO guardrail spec + get PM signoff (ETA 72h)

Jordan Lee: good. Monitoring board updated. I'll keep this thread as the canonical incident thread. Please add any customer-specific notes.

Jordan Lee: quick status 8:49 UTC — mitigation in place, p99 trending down to ~420ms, continuing to observe. If anyone sees regressions or rollout failures ping here. :thumbsup:
